# fpga-project

RTL is written in Verilog and verified with **cocotb** on open-source simulators.
**Vivado** is only used to build the bitstream, from a project generated by script.

| Task | Tool | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Simulate / test | cocotb + Icarus Verilog | `make test` |
| Lint | Verilator | `make lint` |
| Open in Vivado | Vivado 2025.1 | `make project` |
| Bitstream | Vivado 2025.1 (batch) | `make bitstream` → `build/out/top.bit` |

## Layout

```
src/hdl/            Verilog sources (one module per file)
src/constraints/    .xdc files
src/ip/<name>/      Vivado IP, .xci only (optional)
tests/              cocotb tests, one test_<module>.py per module
scripts/            settings.tcl (part, top, Vivado version), create_project.tcl, build.tcl
build/              generated Vivado project + outputs (gitignored, safe to delete)
sim_build/          generated simulation builds + waveforms (gitignored)
```

## Setup

**Simulation (everyone):**

```bash
# Linux/WSL: sudo apt install iverilog verilator gtkwave
# macOS:     brew install icarus-verilog verilator gtkwave
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
make test
```

Waveforms are written to `sim_build/<test>/*.fst`. Open them with `gtkwave` or Surfer.

**Bitstream (whoever has Vivado):** install exactly the version in `scripts/settings.tcl`.
The scripts refuse to run on any other version, because a mismatch rewrites IP and project files.

## Workflow

1. Branch off `main`: `git switch -c feature/uart-tx`
2. Write the module in `src/hdl/` and its test in `tests/test_<module>.py`
   (copy `tests/test_counter.py` as a template).
3. `make lint && make test` until green.
4. Open a pull request. CI runs lint and all cocotb tests; a teammate reviews.
5. Squash-merge once CI passes.

Never commit anything from `build/`. If you change settings in the Vivado GUI
(part, top, new files, IP), put the change in `scripts/` or `src/` too, or it is lost
the next time someone regenerates the project.

## Releasing a bitstream

Bitstreams are not committed. After merging, someone with Vivado runs
`make bitstream` on `main` and attaches `build/out/top.bit` to a GitHub Release
tagged with the commit (e.g. `v0.3.0`). The build fails if timing is not met.

## Adding Vivado IP

Create the IP in the GUI with its location set to `src/ip/<ip_name>/`, and turn off
"core container". Commit only the `.xci`; `create_project.tcl` regenerates the rest.
Note that cocotb can't simulate Xilinx IP on Icarus, so keep IP at the edges of the
design (clocking, memories) and test the logic around it.
